title: The Bank of Russia increases the key rate by 100 b.p. to 9.50% p.a.
claim: The Bank of Russia raised the key rate because inflation was above forecast and demand was outpacing output capacity.
source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank press release with clear dated policy action and rationale.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material. The Bank of Russia is operationally independent, yet it was acting within Putin's wartime state environment.
contrary_evidence: The wider economy still faced sanctions and later recession pressures.

title: Bank of Russia increases the key rate to 20% p.a.
claim: The Bank of Russia hiked the key rate to 20% to support financial and price stability and protect household savings from depreciation.
source_confidence_reason: Primary policy announcement with explicit rationale and immediate macro-stabilization intent.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material through the regime's monetary authority; the action occurred under Putin's invasion and sanctions shock.
contrary_evidence: The need for an emergency hike itself indicates severe instability after the invasion and sanctions.

title: The Bank of Russia keeps the key rate at 20% p.a.
claim: The central bank said the 28 February hike and capital controls helped support stable functioning of the financial system, while it kept the key rate at 20%.
source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank statement describing crisis measures and their stated effect.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; the bank acted under war-induced financial stress, not as a neutral peacetime actor.
contrary_evidence: The same release says external conditions had changed drastically and threatened financial stability.

title: The Bank of Russia cuts the key rate by 300 b.p. to 14.00% p.a.
claim: The bank cut the rate to 14%, projected 2022 inflation at 18.0-23.0%, and forecast GDP to fall 8.0-10.0% in 2022.
source_confidence_reason: Primary macro-policy release with specific forecasts and policy response.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material via the central bank's wartime stabilization role under Putin's state.
contrary_evidence: The bank still expected a severe contraction and sustained inflation.

title: Monetary Policy Guidelines for 2022-2024
claim: The Bank of Russia stated that price stability close to 4% is its main goal and that forecast-based decisions and transparency are core monetary-policy principles.
source_confidence_reason: Primary policy framework document describing stated objectives and tools.
period_fit: pre-2022 baseline for target-period monetary policy
ruler_attribution: Indirect context only; this is the framework Putin governed through, not a discrete ruler action in 2022.
contrary_evidence: The framework does not itself prove competent execution in 2022.

title: Putin tips central bank chief Nabiullina for third term to ensure economic stability
claim: Putin proposed reappointing Elvira Nabiullina for another term, explicitly framing the move as a bid to preserve macroeconomic stability.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a dated personnel decision; syndicated on Investing.com but the claim is specific and contemporaneous.
ruler_attribution: Direct. This is a Putin-driven appointment signal about who would manage macro policy.
contrary_evidence: Nabiullina still operated within a coercive wartime environment and could not set external policy conditions.

title: Putin orders new budget rules to boost Russia's growth
claim: Putin ordered new budget rules to support growth and said the rules should ensure stability of public finances and raise growth rates.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a specific Kremlin-directed policy instruction; clear ruler attribution and date.
ruler_attribution: Direct. Putin personally ordered the budget-rule work.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes Russia had suspended its prior budget rule and faced sanctions-driven reserve constraints.

title: Russia to restrict budget data in response to Western sanctions
claim: Russia's finance ministry said it would partially restrict public budget-spending information in response to sanctions; the report also said Putin had pledged fresh social payments and that the National Wealth Fund would support key state enterprises.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on government and finance-ministry actions with direct policy detail.
ruler_attribution: Direct for the social-payment pledge and broader fiscal direction; indirect for the finance-ministry disclosure restriction.
contrary_evidence: Restricting budget data reduces transparency and can obscure who benefits from spending.

title: Russia increases its emergency spending fund by $4.6b
claim: Russia increased its emergency spending fund to ensure economic stability under sanctions and had already pledged more than 1 trillion roubles in anti-crisis support to businesses, social payments, and families with children.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report republished by a major outlet; the claim is specific and dated, with direct policy content.
ruler_attribution: Direct for the government's emergency fiscal response under Putin's authority.
contrary_evidence: The same report says sanctions cut Russia off from the global financial system and supply channels.

title: Russia's Putin calls for pension hike above inflation rate
claim: Putin called for an 8.6% pension increase above inflation and had previously ordered one-off social payments and public-sector salary hikes worth at least 500 billion roubles.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on a clear Putin-directed social-spending choice, republished by Euronews.
ruler_attribution: Direct. Putin personally directed the pension and social-payment policy.
contrary_evidence: Analysts said the hikes could further fuel inflation.

title: Putin orders benefit payments for people arriving in Russia from Ukraine
claim: Putin signed a decree establishing monthly pension payments and other benefits for people forced to leave Ukrainian territory for Russia.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on a dated decree with precise benefit terms and direct ruler action.
ruler_attribution: Direct. This was a Putin-signed benefits decree.
contrary_evidence: The policy is narrow and conflict-linked rather than broad-based prosperity policy.

title: Putin says Russia will post budget surplus this year, GDP to decline 'around 2%'
claim: Putin said Russia would post a budget surplus in 2022 and forecast GDP would fall around 2%, a milder contraction than earlier expected.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters coverage of Putin's public economic forecast and budget claim, republished by Euronews.
ruler_attribution: Direct. The claim is Putin's own public economic assessment.
contrary_evidence: His optimism was more upbeat than the economy ministry and major banks, and it rested partly on energy-revenue windfalls.

title: Russia's 2022 economic fall seen in lower incomes, slumping consumer demand
claim: Russian consumer demand contracted at its fastest pace in seven years in 2022, real disposable incomes fell 1%, and retail sales slumped 6.7%.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting on Rosstat data with specific household and demand indicators for 2022.
period_fit: retrospective evidence for the 2022 target year
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; these are economy-wide outcomes under Putin's wartime policy environment.
contrary_evidence: Unemployment stayed at a record low, showing some labor-market resilience.

title: Russian unemployment rate hits record low, economic data paints mixed picture
claim: Russia's unemployment fell to a record low 3.8%, but real wages fell 3.2% year on year in July and car production dropped 69%.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report on Rosstat data with concrete labor-market and output figures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material; the mixed labor-market result came under Putin's sanctions-era policy mix and mobilization shock.
contrary_evidence: Low unemployment partly reflected labor shortages after mobilization and emigration, not broad prosperity.

title: IMF Staff Statement on the Economic Impact of War in Ukraine
claim: The IMF said sanctions on the Russian Central Bank would severely restrict access to reserves, disrupt cross-border transactions, and that fiscal policy should support the most vulnerable households.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF statement issued immediately after the invasion with direct macro-financial assessment.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong. The consequences flowed from Putin's invasion and the regime's response environment.
contrary_evidence: The IMF was describing macro damage and policy needs, not praising Russian performance.

title: War Dims Global Economic Outlook as Inflation Accelerates
claim: The IMF projected steep contractions for Russia and said the war and sanctions were increasing inflation and hurting lower-income households through food and fuel prices.
source_confidence_reason: Official IMF analysis with explicit Russia-specific macro projections and distributional effects.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong. The forecast explicitly ties Russia's contraction to Putin's war and sanctions.
contrary_evidence: The same piece notes some commodity exporters benefited from higher energy and food prices.

title: WEO Update July 2022 Press Briefing Transcript
claim: The IMF said Russia's domestic economy had been doing fairly well because emergency financial and monetary measures helped stabilize the financial sector, even though the projected 2022 contraction was still 6%.
source_confidence_reason: Official IMF transcript with Russia-specific forecast revision and explanation of short-run stabilization.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material. The stabilization reflects the regime's macro response after Putin's invasion.
contrary_evidence: The same transcript still describes a severe recession and worsening 2023 outlook.

title: Financial Stability Review, May 2022
claim: The ECB said sanctions had significantly isolated Russia's economy and were reflected in a sharp downgrade of its growth outlook and higher inflation expectations.
source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank analysis from a major international institution with explicit Russia assessment.
ruler_attribution: Indirect macro context tied to Putin's invasion and the sanctions response.
contrary_evidence: This is external analysis, not a Russian policy document.

title: OECD Economic Outlook, Interim Report March 2022
claim: The OECD said sanctions cut Russia off from foreign capital and reserves, the ruble depreciated sharply, the policy rate rose to 20%, and the downturn in Russia could be larger than after Crimea.
source_confidence_reason: Primary OECD analysis with explicit Russia-specific macro and financial-system effects.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but strong. The report links these effects to Putin's invasion and the sanctions it triggered.
contrary_evidence: Russia had some energy-revenue cushion and many domestic effects depended on sanctions intensity.

title: Russia: Freedom in the World 2022 Country Report
claim: Freedom House described Putin's system as centralized and corrupt, with elites receiving government contracts and protection in return for loyalty, and said the Kremlin manipulates elections and suppresses dissent.
locator: overview and C2 section, lines 80-82 and 151-152
source_confidence_reason: Major rights-monitoring assessment with clear Russia-wide institutional and corruption findings.
ruler_attribution: Direct and indirect. The report ties corruption and patronage to Putin's personalist system.
contrary_evidence: The report also notes that the regime maintains formal institutions and elections, albeit heavily manipulated.

title: Russia: Nations in Transit 2022 Country Report
claim: Freedom House said corruption among Russian elites is omnipresent, that access to officials' financial information was constrained by presidential decree, and that anti-corruption rules were being used to tighten control rather than increase oversight.
source_confidence_reason: Detailed country report from a major democracy monitor with specific corruption and transparency findings.
ruler_attribution: Direct and indirect. The report describes presidentially ordered transparency constraints and elite corruption under Putin.
contrary_evidence: Russia also retained formal anti-corruption plans and some prosecutions, but the report says these were selective and politically useful.

title: Treasury Sanctions Russians Bankrolling Putin and Russia-Backed Influence Actors
claim: Treasury said Russian elites and family members were providing direct and indirect support to Putin's government and war, and that sanctions targeted disinformation outlets and defense enterprises.
source_confidence_reason: Primary sanctions release from a major government source with specific designated-network claims.
ruler_attribution: Indirect. This is external corroboration of Putin-linked elite networks rather than a Russian policy act.
contrary_evidence: It reflects foreign sanctions action, not a domestic reform or welfare policy.

title: Russian Elites, Proxies, and Oligarchs Task Force Joint Statement
claim: The REPO task force said it had immobilized about $300 billion in Russian Central Bank assets and blocked or frozen more than $30 billion in sanctioned Russian assets.
source_confidence_reason: Primary multinational sanctions statement with concrete figures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect macro constraint from the sanctions environment created by Putin's invasion.
contrary_evidence: These are foreign countermeasures, not evidence of Putin's economic stewardship by themselves.

title: World Bank Group Statement on Russia and Belarus
claim: The World Bank said it stopped all its programs in Russia and Belarus immediately after the invasion.
source_confidence_reason: Primary institution statement describing a direct institutional response to the invasion.
ruler_attribution: Indirect consequence of Putin's invasion and the resulting isolation of Russia.
contrary_evidence: This is an external institutional response, not a domestic policy choice.

title: Putin tips central bank chief Nabiullina for third term to ensure economic stability
claim: Putin proposed nominating Elvira Nabiullina for a third term as Bank of Russia governor to ensure macroeconomic stability and preserve the central bank's inflation-fighting role.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting with direct attribution and clear policy context.
period_fit: Target-period 2022; direct March 2022 personnel decision inside the ruler period.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin proposal, although implementation still depended on parliamentary confirmation and central-bank action.
contrary_evidence: Stability still depended heavily on emergency controls and sanctions-driven trade revenues.

title: Putin orders new budget rules to boost Russia's growth
claim: Putin ordered the government to draw up new budget rules to boost growth and protect the economy from a serious downturn, saying the rules should stabilize public finances and raise growth rates.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters report with a direct Putin quote and clear dated policy action.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin instruction on fiscal rules and macro strategy.
contrary_evidence: The rule change unfolded under sanctions pressure and a war-driven downturn, so it was partly reactive stabilization rather than clean long-run reform.

title: Putin throws lifeline to housing sector with subsidised mortgages extension
claim: Putin extended Russia's preferential mortgage scheme across the country until July 1, 2024, raising the subsidized rate to 8% from 7% and keeping 6% mortgages for families with at least two children.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report with direct Putin quote and concrete program terms.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin decision affecting household credit access and construction demand.
contrary_evidence: The measure was a targeted subsidy to support a strained sector, not a structural fix to broader growth weaknesses.

title: Putin orders benefit payments for people arriving in Russia from Ukraine
claim: Putin signed a decree introducing financial benefits for people forced to leave Ukrainian territory for Russia, including monthly pension payments of 10,000 roubles and one-off support for pregnant women and disabled people.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters report based on a government portal decree and direct presidential attribution.
ruler_attribution: Direct Putin order, though the policy is conflict-linked and targeted at displaced people from occupied or Russian-linked areas.
contrary_evidence: The measure is narrow and conflict-tied, so it does not by itself show broad prosperity policy.

title: On 2022 year a moratorium was introduced on some planned inspections of SMEs
claim: A rule applicable in 2022 imposed a moratorium on some planned inspections of small and medium-sized businesses, with exceptions for high-risk activity and some licensing and audit cases.
source_confidence_reason: Legal summary of a formal government decree; the rule is explicit even though the page is a secondary legal digest.
period_fit: Rule applied in 2022; source published in 2021 as a legal summary of the 2022 inspection moratorium.
ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution through the government regulatory regime under Putin, not a personal presidential act in this source.
contrary_evidence: High-risk and some licensable activities remained subject to inspection, so the moratorium was partial rather than blanket deregulation.

title: Russia's 2022 economic fall seen in lower incomes, slumping consumer demand
claim: Reuters reported Rosstat data showing Russian consumer demand contracted at its fastest pace in seven years in 2022, real disposable incomes fell 1%, and retail sales fell 6.7%.
source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters summary of official Rosstat data with clear quantitative claims.
ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Putin-era policy and war shock, but strongly confounded by sanctions, mobilization, and external market conditions.
contrary_evidence: Unemployment remained at a record low 3.7%, so the household picture was mixed rather than uniformly collapsing.

title: Russian consumer inflation slows to 12% as central bank meeting looms
claim: Annual inflation in Russia slowed to 11.98% in November 2022, still far above the Bank of Russia's 4% target, and Reuters noted that households viewed inflation as a major living-standards concern.
source_confidence_reason: Reuters-sourced release of official Rosstat inflation data with a precise annual figure.
period_fit: Target-period 2022; November 2022 inflation snapshot inside the ruler period.
ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution, because war, sanctions, and monetary tightening all contributed to the inflation path.
contrary_evidence: The inflation rate was falling from earlier peaks, so the year showed stabilization as well as severe price pressure.

title: Rosstat adjusts Russian poverty level for 2022 to 9.8% from 10.5%
claim: RBC reported that Rosstat revised 2022 poverty to 9.8% and said the income ratio between the top 10% and bottom 10% fell to 13.8, attributing the improvement to targeted social support and higher transfers.
source_confidence_reason: Report cites Rosstat's revised 2022 figures and explicitly links the change to targeted support measures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but material attribution through Putin-era social spending and transfer policy; not a clean ruler-only causal proof.
contrary_evidence: The improvement occurred amid war, sanctions, and a real-income squeeze, so it is not a clean prosperity boom.

title: WEO Update July 2022 Press Briefing Transcript
claim: The IMF said Russia's domestic economy had been doing fairly well because measures taken at the onset of the war, especially on the financial and monetary side, were effective, and strong oil and gas export revenues also helped support the outlook.
source_confidence_reason: Primary IMF transcript quoting IMF staff directly and tying performance to early stabilization measures.
ruler_attribution: Indirect attribution, since the IMF credits the policy response and export revenues rather than Putin personally, but it is relevant to the ruler-period record.
contrary_evidence: The same IMF answer still described the outlook as a fairly severe recession, not a clean success story.

title: Russia: Nations in Transit 2022 Country Report
claim: Freedom House said Russia remained deeply corrupt and that access to public employees' personal assets and finances had been constrained by presidential decree, which the report said was meant to block independent investigations into grand corruption.
source_confidence_reason: Country report synthesizes the corruption environment and cites the decree-based disclosure restrictions directly.
period_fit: 2022 country report covering the ruler period and its immediate baseline.
ruler_attribution: Indirect but relevant to Putin's control of disclosure rules and elite capture environment.
contrary_evidence: The same report notes an anti-corruption plan existed, so the picture is one of constrained, not absent, anti-corruption governance.

title: Bank of Russia measures to support credit institutions
claim: The Bank of Russia loosened loan-provisioning and capital-buffer rules and recommended restructuring loans to cushion sanctions pressure and keep credit institutions able to lend to the economy.
source_confidence_reason: Primary central-bank press release with explicit dated policy actions and rationale.
ruler_attribution: Institutional and indirect rather than personal-Putin attribution, but still part of the ruler-period economic response architecture.
contrary_evidence: These were emergency defenses against sanctions shock, not evidence of preexisting structural strength.
